reason: Verified by driving state=day at 390x844 and reading render-b.js. Every factual claim holds. In one phone screen the text runs: 'Wedding day at The Orchard' at y=224, then 'Happening now' / 'Wedding day' at y=426-452 (the same words twice, 228px apart, because fixture.js line 81 titles the anchor milestone identically to primaryDate.label on line 89), then the last full sentence before the footer is 'Venue walk-through, 19 September. The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead.', then a footer stamped 'Updated 15 July 2026' read on 3 October 2026. The cancelled 'City hotel shortlist / No date' row is also still printed in the keepsake list. behindBlock() takes a clock but has no day-of branch, and foot() hardcodes the stamp, so the rule written for a guest reading in July runs unchanged on the morning itself. This is not taste: naming a dropped hotel search as the closing sentence of a wedding-morning keepsake, and stamping it eleven weeks stale, is a copy defect on the one screen the brief says the company is judged on, and no automated gate can see it. The fix as written is right in aim but wrong in two of its four moves, so it is sharpened rather than accepted verbatim.
sharpenedFix: Keep moves (1) and (4); replace moves (2) and (3). (1) Delete the .b-dayNote paragraph 'This is the day the plan was for.' — it is the weakest line on the screen and the header already says everything. (2) DO NOT suppress .b-dayNow: interaction-check.mjs:709 asserts /happening now/i on state=day, and the section exists to fix a documented earlier lie (render-b.js comment above states.day). Kill the duplication instead by merging: in states.day, drop the standalone .b-sub line and let the .b-dayNow section carry it, so the block reads 'Happening now' / 'Wedding day at The Orchard' exactly once. Both gate regexes at interaction-check.mjs:708-709 still pass on that single instance; give the merged line the existing .b-sub type treatment so the audit type ramp is unchanged. (3) DO NOT switch the day-of note to a count: render-b.js lines 185-189 deliberately rule that received surfaces name things and never tally, and '8 things got you here' would reinstate the tracker voice on the most received screen in the set. Instead give behindBlock a day-of branch that keeps the naming form and drops only the cancellation: when clock === F.project.primaryDate.date, set note = last.title + ', ' + F.fmt.medium(last.date) + '.' with no dropped clause, relabel .b-behindLabel to 'How you got here', and also filter cancelled items out of the rendered rows on that branch — otherwise 'City hotel shortlist / No date' still sits in the keepsake list and the sentence-level fix is cosmetic. (4) Give foot() an optional stamp flag and pass none on state=day, so the morning footer reads 'Kept by Orla' and 'Signal Timeline' only; no gate asserts the footer stamp. Add gate assertions that state=day contains neither 'Updated' nor 'not going ahead', and that /Wedding day/ occurs exactly once.
